title: Catalog gateway: sponsorship bridge and graceful deprecation clauses for enterprise model requests
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description: Create a lightweight "sponsorship bridge" workflow and formal "graceful deprecation" clauses so enterprise customer requests (new model adds, urgent pin requests, requests to deprecate) are triaged with clear SLAs, rollback runbooks, and eval gate expectations. The goal is to reduce ad-hoc engineering interrupts, improve predictability for enterprise customers, and ensure deprecations do not break pinned production workloads.
proposal_summary: Introduce a two-track intake flow: 1) Sponsor-bridge lane for SLA-backed enterprise requests that require expedited evaluation and potential temporary pinning; 2) Standard catalog intake for normal cadence. Define deprecation notice windows, automated compatibility checks, mandatory eval set signatures for pins, and a rollback/runbook template that engineers can execute without additional research.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Sponsor-bridge form completed in Console that captures sponsor, customer org, impact, suggested pin duration, and required eval set link
A2: Triage SLA: sponsor-bridge items acknowledged within 24h and initial feasibility decision within 3 business days
A3: Automatic compatibility checks run for requested model variant and surface blocking incompatibilities in Console
A4: Graceful deprecation policy documented with minimum notice windows per customer tier and auto-flag for pinned customers
A5: Rollback/runbook template published in Confluence and versioned in GitHub; at least one dry-run completed by Eng on staging
A6: Telemetry dashboard with time_to_onboard, pin_count, post_onboard_incidents, and deprecation_impact (customer pins affected) visible to PM and Eng
decisions: D1: Sponsor-bridge will be opt-in per enterprise customer via Console – requires sponsor approval and legal opt-in
D2: Temporary pins allowed for up to 30 days by default; extensions require documented test/eval signature and PM approval
D3: Compatibility checks will be best-effort static checks + a configurable shadow inference run for high-risk customers
D4: Deprecation notice windows: Hosted customers receive 30 days, Dedicated receive 60 days, Private (on-prem/VPC) receive 90 days
D5: Security review is not mandatory for every sponsor-bridge request but will be required for model variants flagged by static analysis or customer classification
tradeoffs: T1: Faster sponsor-bridge lane increases operational interrupts for Eng but reduces customer friction — mitigated by firm SLAs and temporary pins capped at 30 days
T2: Automated shadow inference increases cost and complexity; we limit full shadow runs to enterprise-tier requests to control spend
T3: Longer deprecation windows protect customers but slow the retirement of unsafe or inefficient models — emergency retirement path retained for severe safety/regulatory issues

eval_gate_requirements: EG1: Signed eval set with >=500 prompts representative of customer traffic for any requested pin >7 days
EG2: Regression checks on critical prompts show <=2% drop in task-level accuracy compared to pinned baseline
EG3: Performance check: 95th percentile latency within agreed SLA band for customer tier
EG4: Privacy check: model variant passes PII leakage scan for customer data patterns
